5.0 Introduction

Energy is one of the most fundamental parts of our universe. We use energy to do work. Energy lights our cities, powers our vehicles, trains, planes and rockets. Energy warms our homes and cooks our food. Energy from the sun gives us light during the day. Energy stored in plants is eaten by animals, giving them energy. Everything we do is related to energy in one way or another. Energy is defined as:
5.0 Introduction

"the ability to do work." When we eat, our bodies transform the energy stored in the food into energy to do work. Cars, planes, light bulbs, boats and machinery also transform energy into work. Where does energy come from? There are many sources of energy. In this chapter we will discuss various aspects of energy, its kinds, conservation and management.
5.1 Energy Sources and their Significance

There are many different ways in which the abundance of energy around us can be stored, converted, and extended for our use. To help understand the key energy sources that will play an important role in the world, the energy sources have been divided into two main categories: non renewable sources and renewable sources. Non renewable sources include the fossil fuels like coal, petroleum, and natural gas.
5.1.1 Fossil Fuels

Conventional energy sources are typically fully developed and include non renewable energy resources like fossil fuels as well as nuclear power, while non-conventional sources, which include renewable energy resources like solar power, hydropower and wind power, may be functional but are still undergoing development.
5.1.1 Fossil Fuels

Fossil fuels are expensive and require established technologies that can produce energy round the clock. Non-conventional energy sources have much smaller environmental impacts and they are renewable. Conventional sources of energy have a limited supply because eventually the nuclear elements and fossil fuels will be used up.
5.1.1 Fossil Fuels

In addition, burning fossil fuels releases significant amounts of greenhouse gases and contributes to environmental pollution. Non-conventional energy sources are still expensive and are often limited to producing energy only under certain circumstances, such as sunny days for solar panels and windy days for windmills. Let's study each source in detail.
5.1.1 Fossil Fuels

Fossil fuels have been widely used as a source of energy since the Industrial Revolution just before the dawn of the 20th century. Fossil fuels are relatively easy to use and it is easy to generate energy from them because they only require a simple direct combustion. However, a problem with fossil fuels is their environmental impact.
5.1.1 Fossil Fuels

Not only does their excavation from the ground significantly alter the environment, but their combustion leads to a great deal of air pollution. Although there are many different types of fossil fuels the most important are: coal, petroleum, and natural
5.1.1 Fossil Fuels

a. Coal: About 300 million years back, a large number of ferns and other prehistoric plants were common on the swamp-like earth. When those plants died and fell to the ground, they were covered with water and they slowly decomposed. As decomposition took place in the absence of oxygen, much of the hydrogen content of the matter was eroded away, leaving a material rich in carbon.
5.1.1 Fossil Fuels

The material was compressed over the years by sand and dirt, leaving the form of carbon known as coal. The nature of coal is such that the higher the carbon content, the more cleanly and brilliantly the coal burns.
5.1.1 Fossil Fuels

The other states of coal, from lowest carbon content to highest, are "lignite," bituminous coal, and anthracite coal. If the coal is heated and compressed even more, the result is "graphite," almost completely pure carbon. Coal is used extensively for the generation of electricity for running industries.
For Your Information

Coal reservoir of Pakistan: Thar desert gives a look of barren and dry harsh landscape. Hidden deep in it lies what can possibly be called the black gold of Pakistan. Thar coal is one of the 5th largest coal reservoirs in the world having a total of about 850 trillion cubic feet of reserves (as printed), which can possibly enable Pakistan to produce enough electricity to power the entire country.
5.1.1 Fossil Fuels

b. Petroleum: Petroleum, or "crude oil," is a liquid fuel that is present in various locations throughout the world. It has many uses, from the generation of electricity to the manufacture of medicines, plastics, and other commercial items. Much like coal, petroleum is formed from the remains of biodegraded organic material.
5.1.1 Fossil Fuels

When animals that lived in the sea millions of years ago died underwater, their remains were gradually covered by layers of very fine dirt known as "silt" on the ocean floor. Then, as the years passed, pressure from the layers built up and compressed the organic material, forming the oil.
5.1.1 Fossil Fuels

c. Natural gas: Natural gas consists primarily of methane (CH4). It is found associated with other hydrocarbon fuel. Natural gas is almost always found along with the deposits of petroleum. When the petroleum is drilled, natural gas is also recovered. Wells with only natural gas also exist. Many houses, offices, and other buildings are heated by natural gas heaters.
5.1.1 Fossil Fuels

The western hemisphere, Europe, and parts of Africa contain the largest natural gas deposits. The gas is usually transported by pipelines. Compared to petroleum and coal, natural gas is relatively clean-burning because it contains only trace portions of sulfur and nitrogen.
For Your Information

Sui Gas Field of Pakistan: Sui is located at a distance of about 650 kilometres (km) from Karachi in Dera Bugti, Balochistan. Sui is a major gas field of Pakistan. As a major production facility, Sui Gas Field (SGF) has the country's largest gas compressor station and a purification plant. At the time of its discovery, SGF was considered among the largest natural gas fields in the world.
For Your Information
Despite diminishing reserves over time, SGF still remains the highest natural gas producing field in Pakistan.
5.1.2 Renewable Energy Sources

Due to diminishing fossil fuels, renewable energy may become a major energy choice for the 21st century. Among the most important of these sources are wind, hydroelectric and solar. Renewable energy sources are environmentally clean and virtually inexhaustible.
5.1.2 Renewable Energy Sources
Their major drawbacks, however, are limited energy production (in most cases not suitable for large-scale power generation) as well as relative cost to build and maintain.
5.1.2 Renewable Energy Sources

a. Wind energy: Wind has been used as a source of energy for centuries. About 3000 BC, people probably first used the force of moving air to push a boat with a sail through the water. This might have led to the invention of the windmills. These windmills were first used in central Asia. Windmills were used in Europe more than 700 years ago to grind grains and pump water.
5.1.2 Renewable Energy Sources
More recently wind power is used to turn wind turbines. In the United States and Europe many wind farms routinely generate several megawatts of electricity a day.
5.1.2 Renewable Energy Sources

Wind Power - Clean Way of Electricity Generation: Wind power is the fastest-growing energy source in the world. Turbines powered by wind are mounted on towers 100 or more feet above the ground, where the wind is faster and less turbulent. (Diagram labels: wind direction, generator, power line, tower.) • In Pakistan efforts are being made to use wind energy for pumping water and producing electricity.
5.1.2 Renewable Energy Sources

b. Hydroelectric energy: Man has utilized the power of water for years. Hydroelectric systems make use of the energy in running water to create electricity. In coal and natural gas systems, a fossil fuel is burned to heat water. The steam pressure from the boiling water turns "propellers" called turbines. These turbines spin coils of wire between magnets to produce electricity.
5.1.2 Renewable Energy Sources

Hydropowered systems also make use of turbines to generate electrical power; however, they do so by using the energy in moving water to spin the turbines. Water has kinetic energy when it flows from higher elevations to lower elevations. This energy spins the turbines and generates electricity. Ghazi Barotha Hydropower Project: Ghazi Barotha Hydropower Project is a unique power project.
5.1.2 Renewable Energy Sources

It has a generation capacity of 1450 MW and it consists of three main components: the Barrage, the Power Channel and the Power Complex. The project utilizes the normal Tarbela Dam releases to provide year round maximum power generation.
5.1.2 Renewable Energy Sources

In Pakistan hydroelectric power projects are contributing significantly to electricity production. Although Pakistan has huge hydel power generation capacity, mainly on river Indus, it has yet to exploit it to its maximum capacity. However, three main dams, Tarbela, Mangla and Warsak, constructed for the purpose of generating electricity and irrigating agricultural land, are vital for the energy sector in Pakistan.
5.1.2 Renewable Energy Sources

c. Solar Energy: Most of the energy known to man is derived in some way from the sun. When we burn wood or other fuels, we actually release the stored energy of the sun. In fact, there would be no life on earth without the sun, which provides energy needed for the growth of plants and, indirectly, the existence of all animal life.
5.1.2 Renewable Energy Sources

Nowadays electric current is obtained from the sun's energy. A device called a solar cell can change the energy of sunlight to electrical energy. Such solar cells are frequently used in calculators, watches etc. Batteries made up of solar cells are used to run radios, televisions and equipment in artificial satellites going around the earth.
5.1.2 Renewable Energy Sources

Solar cookers, solar geysers and solar house heating systems are successfully working by using solar energy. Solar power has an exciting future ahead of it, because solar power utilizes sunlight, a resource that is everywhere. Solar panels can be attached to moving objects, such as automobiles, to power those objects. Solar powered cars are being experimented with these days.
Do You Know?

There are two ways in which solar power can be converted to energy. The first, known as "solar thermal applications," involves using the energy of the sun to directly heat air or a liquid. The second, known as "photoelectric applications," involves the use of photovoltaic cells to convert solar energy directly to electricity.
5.1.3 Nuclear Energy

The diminishing availability of natural resources such as coal, petroleum and crude oil has left scientists searching for an energy alternative. Harnessing the power of the atom appears to be one of the solutions. Fission and fusion reactions are the two types of nuclear reaction with the help of which energy can be produced from an atom.
5.1.3 Nuclear Energy

Nuclear energy is the energy released from the nucleus of the atom when it is hit or bombarded by a slow moving atomic particle called a neutron. When the atom of Uranium-235 is hit by the neutron, it splits up into several parts with the release of an enormous amount of energy; this process is known as nuclear fission. It is carried out in specially designed nuclear reactors.
5.1.3 Nuclear Energy

Cold water is pushed into the core of the nuclear reactor, which carries away heat of the nuclear reactor and turns into steam. The steam is ejected into the steam turbine, which begins to turn the generator to produce electricity.
5.1.3 Nuclear Energy

In Pakistan, Karachi Nuclear Power Plant (KANUPP) and Chashma Nuclear Power Plant (CHASNUPP-1) are the two main nuclear power plants which are producing electricity. KANUPP has a capacity to produce 137 megawatts of electricity. It is located at Paradise Point on the Arabian Sea coast, about 15 miles to the west of Karachi.
5.1.3 Nuclear Energy

CHASNUPP-1, the second nuclear power plant in Pakistan, was started in 1992 with the help of the People's Republic of China. CHASNUPP-1 has a capacity of 325 megawatts of electricity. The plant is located in the province of Punjab near Chashma Barrage on the left bank of River Indus, 32 km south of Mianwali city.
5.1.4 Hydrogen as Fuel

Hydrogen is the simplest element. An atom of hydrogen consists of only one proton and one electron. It is also the most plentiful element in the universe, but it is always present combined with other elements, e.g. water (H2O). Hydrogen is also found in many organic compounds, notably the hydrocarbons that make up many of our fuels, such as gasoline, natural gas, methanol and propane.
5.1.4 Hydrogen as Fuel

Hydrogen can be separated from hydrocarbons through the application of heat - a process known as reforming. Currently, most hydrogen is made in this way from natural gas. An electrical current can also be used to separate water into its components of oxygen and hydrogen. This process is known as electrolysis.
5.1.4 Hydrogen as Fuel
Some algae and bacteria, using sunlight as their energy source, even give off hydrogen under certain conditions.
5.1.4 Hydrogen as Fuel

A fuel cell combines hydrogen and oxygen to produce electricity, heat and water. Fuel cells are often compared to batteries. Both convert the energy produced by a chemical reaction into usable electric power. Fuel cells are useful as a source of heat and electricity for buildings, and as an electrical power source for electric motors propelling vehicles.
5.1.4 Hydrogen as Fuel
Fuel cells operate best on pure hydrogen, but fuels like natural gas, methanol, or even gasoline can be reformed to produce the hydrogen required for fuel cells.
5.1.4 Hydrogen as Fuel

Hydrogen Fuel in Space Shuttle: Hydrogen is high in energy, yet an engine that burns pure hydrogen produces almost no pollution. NASA has used liquid hydrogen since the 1970s to propel the space shuttle and other rockets into orbit. Hydrogen fuel cells power the shuttle's electrical systems, producing a clean byproduct - pure water, which is used by the crew for drinking.
5.3 Measurement of Energy

Worldwide, two systems of units of measurement are commonly used today: the Metric System (Systeme International) and the British System. Energy can be converted into work. Energy can be represented by the following simple equation:
5.3 Measurement of Energy

Work = Force x Distance Energy is defined as the ability to do work. However, work is defined as a force applied to some form of matter (object) multiplied by the distance that this object travels. Physicists commonly describe force with a unit of measurement known as a newton (after Sir Isaac Newton).
5.3 Measurement of Energy

A newton is equal to the force needed to accelerate (move) a mass weighing one kilogram to a distance of one meter in one second in a vacuum with no friction. The work or energy required to move an object with the force of one newton over a distance of one meter is called a joule.
Key Points
Energy is defined as "the ability to do work."

a. Measurement of electricity: The electric meter is connected with the live wire of the main supply. The live wire is connected with the field coils of the meter. Inside the field coil, there is another coil, which can rotate about its axis. When current passes through the meter, a magnetic field is produced due to which the coil inside the field rotates.
Key Points

5.3 Energy in Development of a Country

Energy has become a fundamental aspect of human existence. The development of a country can be judged by the amount of energy it consumes. Generally we see that a developed country has a larger demand for energy compared to a developing or under developed country. Modern day industries cannot sustain their activities without uninterrupted energy supplies.
5.3 Energy in Development of a Country

This in turn ensures the creation of employment opportunities, which ultimately generate economic activities and increase the standard of life of a nation. Development in the fields of agriculture, health, education, industry etc. requires energy, and lack of investment in terms of energy in these fields means no development and a low standard of life.
5.3 Energy in Development of a Country
Access to energy is therefore a prerequisite for sustainable development.
5.3 Energy in Development of a Country

Pakistan's economy is growing steadily. This growth demands higher energy consumption. Pakistan mainly depends upon oil and gas resources to fulfill energy requirements. Indigenous resources of oil are not enough for the growing economy. As a result Pakistan has to import large quantities of oil and oil based products from Middle East countries.
5.3 Energy in Development of a Country

Although Pakistan is blessed with a huge potential for hydel energy, proper planning and a clear strategy in this regard have yet to be devised. Pakistan's total primary energy supply during the year 2007-2008 was 62.88 MTOE (million tons of oil equivalent).
5.3 Energy in Development of a Country

More than 99% of this energy was supplied through conventional energy sources such as oil, gas, hydel and nuclear etc., whereas less than 1% was supplied through micro/mini renewable energy (RE). Today, only 55% of Pakistan's population has access to electricity.
5.3 Energy in Development of a Country

The nation is currently facing the worst power supply shortage ever to hit the country. The occurrence of prolonged and frequent power breakdowns has had a negative impact on industry operation, the economy and the livelihood of citizens in general. While the energy shortage continues to grow, abundant indigenous sustainable energy resources such as wind, solar and biomass remain virtually untapped.
5.3 Energy in Development of a Country
Currently, approximately 66% of power generation in Pakistan is derived from fossil fuels (primarily oil and gas), followed by hydroelectricity (30%) and nuclear energy (3%).
5.4 Energy and Environment

Humans are always in search of different sources of energy to make their lives comfortable and stable, but sometimes these sources of energy become hazardous to them and their environment. Humans are at risk whether it is burning of fossil fuels or production of electricity through a nuclear power plant. Emissions and contaminations all pose serious consequences on the lives of humans.
5.4 Energy and Environment
In the following section we will see how production of energy from various sources affects our lives and what the possible remedial measures are in this regard.
5.4 Energy and Environment

Thermal pollution: The word therm means heat, and heat is a form of energy. It is the kinetic energy associated with the motion of atoms and molecules. A thermal process is that process in which heat is produced or is converted into other forms of energy.
5.4 Energy and Environment

In this process heat exchange between system and surroundings may occur. A combustion reaction is an example of a thermal process. In a combustion reaction carbon dioxide (CO2), water (H2O), light and heat are produced. If oxygen supply to the reaction is insufficient, then carbon monoxide (CO) may also be produced. Certain fuels also contain sulphur. When they burn, sulphur dioxide (SO2) is given off.
5.4 Energy and Environment

Coal and fuel oil contain up to 3% sulphur and petrol about 0.05%. Quite a low concentration of SO2 can damage the leaves of plants and stunt their growth, and it can also make people's respiratory illness much worse. Carbon monoxide (CO) is poisonous and can cause death, even if its concentration is in decimals.
5.4 Energy and Environment
High concentration of CO2 also has adverse effects on the environment; it helps in increasing the temperature of our atmosphere due to the greenhouse effect.
5.4 Energy and Environment
Remedial measures (thermal pollution):
5.4 Energy and Environment

Maximizing the efficiency of heat engines to minimize heat loss. • Less burning of fossil fuels and avoiding energy wastage. • Industries and factories should follow strict norms to reduce thermal pollution. • Temperature of industrial waste water from power plants, paper industries and cement industries should be reduced by the adoption of cooling ponds and towers.
5.4 Energy and Environment

Nuclear Fuel Hazards: Radioactive materials emit certain radiations. These radiations have the ability to penetrate gases, liquids and even solids. The radiations are: 1) alpha radiations, 2) beta radiations, 3) gamma radiations. The penetration power of these radiations is different due to their size, velocity and nature.
5.4 Energy and Environment

Controlled nuclear reactions are useful for humanity, but when they are out of control or when they occur in the open, they damage the whole area. These rays are carcinogenic (causing cancer) and also cause deformation in newborn babies.
5.4 Energy and Environment

Remedial measures: To avoid such hazards, care must be taken in performing nuclear reactions and disposing of nuclear wastes. The design of the nuclear reactor must include provisions for human (operator) error and equipment failure.
5.4 Energy and Environment

Famous accidents of civil nuclear power generation: The three significant accidents in the 50-year history of civil nuclear power generation are: • Three Mile Island (USA 1979), where the reactor was severely damaged but radiation was contained and there were no adverse health or environmental consequences. • Chernobyl (Ukraine 1986): on 26 April 1986, reactor no. 4 of the Chernobyl nuclear power station exploded.
5.4 Energy and Environment
One hundred times more radiation was released than by the atom bombs dropped over Hiroshima and Nagasaki. •
5.4 Energy and Environment

Fukushima (Japan 2011): Fukushima Daiichi nuclear power plant, 150 miles northeast of Tokyo, was severely damaged by the earthquake and tsunami - the world's worst nuclear accident in 25 years. In any nuclear reactor some sort of cooling is necessary. Generally nuclear reactors use water as a coolant; however, some reactors which cannot use water use sodium or sodium salts.
5.4 Energy and Environment
There is a series of physical barriers between the radioactive core and the environment.
5.5 Energy Consumption and Conservation

After obtaining preliminary information, you would have realized the value and importance of energy in modern society. You may have also noticed that conventional sources of energy are limited. Exploitation of non-conventional energy sources is still in the initial stages of research and development.
5.5 Energy Consumption and Conservation

The fuel that burns in factories and transport vehicles or performs other activities is mainly obtained from underground deposits in the form of coal, oil, natural gas and other similar raw forms. These deposits are rapidly decreasing.
5.5 Energy Consumption and Conservation

The rapid growth in population increases the pressure on the use of resources. The excessive and unwise use of resources affects the environment. After all, one day all the resources of energy will be exhausted. It is therefore highly important for us to avoid wastage of energy and conserve energy by taking suitable steps at our homes, schools, industries and offices etc.
5.5 Energy Consumption and Conservation

Conservation of energy in homes: To conserve energy at homes, we must put off the electrical appliances and close gas and water valves when not required. We should use electrical appliances that use comparatively less energy, e.g. tube lights, energy saver bulbs etc. We should design our homes such that we get maximum benefits of sunlight and proper ventilation.
5.5 Energy Consumption and Conservation

Conservation of energy in schools: We must take steps to minimize energy consumption, like designing schools such that they are properly ventilated and get maximum benefits of the sunlight. • Conservation of energy in industries: Industries play an important role in the development of a country. These industries run with consumption of energy.
5.5 Energy Consumption and Conservation
Although they need a huge amount of energy, consumption of energy could be minimized by better management, reuse of by-products and proper maintenance of machinery.

INTRODUCTION

1.1 UNDERSTANDING THE PROBLEM

To solve a given problem by using a computer, you need to write a program for it. To write a computer program, you must know two things: what you want the computer to do, and a means to tell the computer what you want it to do. The first part (also known as algorithm development) is often far more difficult than the second.
1.1 UNDERSTANDING THE PROBLEM
For this reason, many tools (such as flowcharts and pseudo code) have been developed to help with this process.
1.1.1 The Problem
A problem is an obstacle, difficulty or challenge, or any situation that needs to be solved.
1.1.1 The Problem

When there is a difference between what "should be" and what "is"; then a problem occurs. To make the problem definition easy, ask yourself some questions. For example, if you want to write a program to "find the average of five numbers" you can ask yourself following questions:
1.1.1 The Problem
What does average exactly means?
1.1.1 The Problem
How to calculate the average value?
1.1.1 The Problem
In this way the problem can be well-defined precisely.
1.1.2 Problem Analysis

A computer is not that much intelligent that it can analyze a problem and come up with a solution by its own. That is the human (the programmer) who must analyze the problem, develop the instructions for solving the problem, and then use the computer to execute the instructions to solve the problem.
1.1.2 Problem Analysis
After selecting and describing a problem, you need to define the causes.
To analyze the causes:

You need a clear idea of the problem so that it can be analyzed. • Revisit the problem description to make sure you are clear about: • What is the problem about? • How frequently does it occur? • When and where does it occur? • Who is affected? • Brainstorm the possible causes. • Group the causes together.
To analyze the causes:
Represent the causes graphically. • After understanding and analyzing the problem, you can move onto planning the solution.
1.1.3 Plan the Solution of Problem
After analysis, the solution of problem is planned. There can be various solutions for a problem but the proposed solution should be cost-effective, time-efficient, speedy and less complex.
1.1.3 Plan the Solution of Problem
The following are some useful problem solving techniques:
1.1.3 Plan the Solution of Problem

Abstraction: solving the problem in a model of the system before applying it to the real system. • Analogy: using a solution that solved a similar problem. • Brainstorming: It is a group creativity technique by which efforts are made to find a conclusion for a specific problem by gathering a list of ideas spontaneously contributed by its members.
1.1.3 Plan the Solution of Problem

Divide and conquer: breaking down a large, complex problem into smaller, solvable problems. • Reduction: transforming the problem into another problem for which solutions exist. • Research: search for already solved problem and their solution. • Trial-and-error: testing possible solutions until the right one is found.
1.1.4 Candid Solution of a Problem

Solution is "the act or process of solving a problem", to obtain the desired optimal result with minimum cost. There may be several alternatives for solving the problem. However, finding "the best" and "the most suited" solution is called candid solution of the problem.
1.1.5 Selecting the best solution
The following factors are very important in selecting the best solution of any problem.
1.1.5 Selecting the best solution
Speed • Cost • Complexity
a. Speed
To develop an efficient solution for solving the problems, the time it uses is the major measure of the efficiency of that solution.
b. Cost
Cost of a solution includes, space and other hardware and software requirements. The solution will be considered to be the best one if it gives optimal desired result with minimum cost.
c. Complexity
Complexity of the solution means the resources required by the solution, most commonly known as the *time* -- how many steps it needs and the *space* -- how much memory it takes.
1.2.1 An Algoritm

An Algorithm is a well-defined step by step process to solve particular problem. Informally, an algorithm is any well-defined computational procedure that takes some value, or set of values, as input and produces some value, or set of values, as output. An algorithm is thus a sequence of computational steps that transform the input into the output.
1.2.1 An Algoritm
We can also view an algorithm as a tool for solving a well-specified computational problem.
1.2.2 Role of Algorithm in Problem solving

Algorithm plays an important role in developing solution to a problem. For example, if we have a complex situation which requires a lot of information to be gathered and a lot of data to be processed. Then by dividing each activity of this information gathering and data processing into steps will make the problem solving an easy task.
1.2.2 Role of Algorithm in Problem solving

"*Divide and Conquer Rule*" a very famous rule that makes the problem solving an easy task. For instance let we take an example of finding the average of 20 numbers. If this process is defined in small discrete steps then we can make the solution very easily.

1.2.3 Criteria for measuring efficiency of an Algorithm
In computer science, efficiency is used to describe properties of an algorithm relating to how much of various types of resources it consumes.
1.2.3 Criteria for measuring efficiency of an Algorithm
The two most frequently encountered and measurable metrics of an algorithm are:
1.2.3 Criteria for measuring efficiency of an Algorithm
speed or running time - the time it takes for an algorithm to complete, and • 'space' - the memory used by the algorithm during its operation.
1.2.3 Criteria for measuring efficiency of an Algorithm
Furthermore its efficiency can be measured on the basis of following factors.
a. Inputs needed

The amount of time an algorithm takes depends on how large is the input on which the algorithm must operate. For example, multiplying huge matrices takes longer than multiplying small ones, etc. An algorithm might take different amounts of time on inputs of the same size.
b. Processing to be completed
The time required to complete the operation is a measure for efficiency of an algorithm. The process completion time is composed of cycle time, wait time and processing time.
c. Decision to be taken
Problem solving and decision-making are important skills to improve the efficiency of an algorithm and get optimal result.
d. Outputs to be provided
An algorithm is said to be correct if, for every input instance, it ends with the correct output.
d. Outputs to be provided

An incorrect algorithm might not end at all on some input instances, or it might end with an output other than the desired one. So the algorithmic solution that provides correct desired output will be considered as the best solution for the problem to be solved.

2.1 INTRODUCTION TO PROGRAMMING

A computer is a device that follows the instructions given to it. A well-defined set of instructions given to the computer is called a computer program. Computer programming is the process of writing a computer program to solve a particular problem. There are many languages such as C, C++, Java, etc., each having its own features.
2.1 INTRODUCTION TO PROGRAMMING
Computer program controls the operation of a computer and it is developed in a computer language to perform a task.
2.1.1 Computer program

A set of instruction that tells a computer what to do is called program. A computer works according to the given instructions in the program. A computer program is written in a programming language. Computer languages are also known as programming languages. A person who develops a program is called programmer.
2.1.1 Computer program

The programmer develops programs to instruct the computer how to process data to convert it into information. A programming language is a means of communication between a user and computer. The following two terms are associated with a program.
Program Syntax

Syntax refers to the rules that define the structure of a language. Syntax in computer programming means the rules that control the structure of the symbols, punctuation, and words of a programming language. Syntax of a programming language is similar to the grammar of a natural language. For example, in C language the output is presented using *printf()* statement, whose syntax is :
Program Syntax
printf("escape sequence/format specifier/string", variable/expression/constant);
Program Semantic

Semantics is the study of meaning in language. It can be applied to entire texts or to single words. It describes the sequence of steps to be performed by a computer when executing the statements of a computer program. For example, the following statement of a C program will multiply two variables x and y and store the result in variable *product*.
2.1.2 Programming Languages

A set of words, symbols and codes used to write programs is called programming language. Different kinds of languages have been developed to perform different types of work on the computer. These languages are used to solve business problems, scientific problems and other general type of problems. Programming languages can be classified into two categories.
2.1.2 Programming Languages
Low level languages • High level languages
Low Level languages

A computer cannot understand instructions given to it in high-level languages or in English. It can only understand and execute instructions given in the form of machine language i.e., binary. These languages are near to computer hardware. Computer can understands these languages easily. Writing a program in low level languages requires a deep knowledge of the internal structure of computer hardware.
Low Level languages
There are two types of low-level languages.
1. Machine language

A type of language in which instructions are written in binary form is called machine language. It is basically the only language that a computer can understands directly. Program written in machine language can be executed rapidly by the computer. Machine language is represented inside the computer by a string of binary digits (bits) 0 and 1.
1. Machine language

The symbol 0 stands for the absence of an electric pulse and the 1 stands for the presence of an electric pulse. Machine language is difficult for human to understand. Machine language is also known as first generation language.
2. Assembly language

Assembly language is a low-level language. It is one step higher than machine language. In assembly language, symbols are used instead of binary code. These symbols are called *mnemonics*. For example, *sub* instruction is used to subtract two numbers.
2. Assembly language

It is also called symbolic language. Programs written in assembly language are easier to write and modify than machine language. The instructions of the assembly language are converted to machine codes by a language translator called assembler and then they are executed by the computer. Assembly language is also known as second generation language.
High Level Languages

High level languages use formats that are similar to English. The purpose of developing high level languages was to enable people to write programs easily, in their own native language environment (English).
High Level Languages

High level languages basically use English words and/or mathematical symbols rather than mnemonic codes. There are different types of high level languages each having its own rules or grammar for writing programs. The program written in high level language must be translated to machine code before executed by the computer. Each high level language has its own translator program.
High Level Languages
Some examples of high level languages are *FORTRAN, C, C++* and *Java*.
High Level Languages
High level programming languages are divided into the following categories.
High Level Languages
Procedural languages • Structured languages • Object-Oriented Programming languages
Procedural languages

Procedural languages are also known as Third Generation Languages (3GLs). In a procedural language, a program is designed using procedures (also called modules). A *procedure* is a sequence of instructions having a unique name.
Procedural languages
Procedures are executed with the reference of their names. Any procedure is defined once but can be used as many times as required within the program.
Procedural languages
Some examples of procedural languages are FORTRAN, Pascal, C and BASIC.
Structured languages
A programming language where the program may be broken down into blocks or procedures, thus allowing a top-down design approach, is called structured language.
Structured languages
Some of the better known structured programming languages are ALGOL, Pascal, PL/I and ADA.
Object Oriented Programming languages

In Object Oriented Programming, the program is developed by using a set of objects. An *object* is a component of program that has a set of modules and data structures. It is a modern and easy technique to design the program. Once an object for any program is designed, it can be re-used in any other program. Some popular and commonly used Object Oriented Programming (OOP) languages are C++ and JAVA.
2.1.3 Characteristics of High Level Languages
The following are some common characteristics of High Level Language.
Easy to Learn
The high-level languages are easier to learn than low-level languages. The statements written for the program are similar to English like statements.
Easy to Understand
The program written in high-level language by one programmer can easily be understood by another programmer because the program instructions are similar to the English language.
Easy to Write Program
In high-level language, a new program can easily be written in a very short time. The larger and complicated software can be developed in few days or months.
Easy to Detect & Remove Errors
The errors in a program can be easily detected and removed. Mostly the errors are occurred during the compilation of new program.
Built-in Library Functions

Each high-level language provides a large number of built-in functions or procedures that can be used to perform specific tasks during designing of new programs. In this way, a lot of time of programmer is saved.
Machine Independence
Program written in high-level language is machine independent. It means that a program written on one type of computer can be executed on another type of computer.
C Language

C is a general-purpose computer programming language developed in 1972 by Dennis Ritchie at AT&T Bell Laboratories of USA. C is a simple and structure oriented programming language. It is a procedural programming language. It is highly portable among platforms and therefore widely used in industry and among computer professionals. The operating system UNIX was written in C.
C Language
(Photograph) Dennis Ritchie: father of the C language
C++ Language

C++ was developed in early 1980s by Bjarne Stroustrup. It is an Object- Oriented Programming (OOP) language. It is an extension of C language. C++ includes all the elements of the C language and it has additional features for working with objects, classes, events and other object-oriented concepts. Most of the application programs, such as word processers and spreadsheets are developed in C++.
Visual Programming Languages

The term visual programming refers to creating or developing Windows-based applications or Graphical User Interface (GUI) applications. The visual programming languages, sometimes called fifth-generation languages, are object-oriented programming languages. These languages provide visual or graphical interface facilities to develop GUI applications.
Visual Programming Languages
Some popular and widely used visual programming languages are Visual Basic (VB) and Visual C++, C# and Java.
C# Language

C# or C-Sharp is an object-oriented programming language. It was developed in 2000 by Microsoft Corporation. It is based on C++ with elements from Visual Basic and Java. It is used to write web applications that can be used across the Internet.
C# Language
All types of programs including games, utilities, operating systems, compilers, business applications and web based applications can be developed in C#.
JAVA Language

Java is a high-level object oriented-programming language developed by Sun Microsystems in 1991. It is very similar to C++ but it is especially used for web page designing. Java Applets are developed in Java language. A Java applet is a small Java program that runs inside another program such as web browser.
JAVA Language
The Java applets are embedded into web pages to rotate images, for animations and to access databases on the Internet.
Compiler

Compiler is a system software that translates high level language source code into machine-language object code. It translates the English like language (Code written in C++) into a Machine language (binary digits 0 and 1) which computers understand directly. The Compiler reads the whole program and translates it into machine language completely. Programming languages like C/C++, Pascal and Java use compiler.
Interpreter

Interpreter is a high-level programming language translator that translates/ and executes the program statement by statement. It converts one program statement into machine language, executes it, and then proceeds to the next statement.
Interpreter

Each time a statement is read, it must be translated into machine language before execution. Compiler translates the entire program into object program before execution by computer. Examples of programming languages that use interpreter are JavaScript, BASIC, Visual Basic and Perl.
2.2 PROGRAMMING ENVIRONMENT

Programming environment is the set of processes and programming tools used to develop computer programs. It includes editor, compiler, linker, debugger, etc. It is called Integrated Development Environment (IDE) for developing computer programs. Integrated Development Environment is application software with a GUI.
2.2.1 Integrated Developement Environment (IDE)

Integrated Development Environment (IDE) is the programming language development tool to create, compile and run programs. IDE is computer software that brings all the processes and tools required for program development into one environment. Today's modern IDEs have user-friendly GUI. C language also uses IDE, as shown in Figure 2.9.

The following are modules of the C programming environment.
1. Editor

Editor or text editor is a program that enables users to create and edit C language source program having extension *.c*, e.g., *student.c* is a C-language source program. Most of the editors automatically highlight compilation errors to easily remove them.
2. Compiler

A compiler is computer software that translates C language program (source program) into machine code (object program) that can be understood and executed by the computer. A compiled C-language program has an extension *.obj*, e.g., student.obj. Compilation process is shown in Figure 2.10.
3. Linker
A computer program that takes one or more object codes generated by a compiler and combines them into a single executable program is called *linker*.
3. Linker

4. Loader
It is a program that loads C-language programs into memory and then executes them.
5. Debugger
In computers, *debugging* is the process of locating and fixing bugs (errors) in computer program code.
5. Debugger

A C-language debugger is a computer program that lets users run the program, line by line and examine the values of variables or look at values passed into functions and helps in finding and removing errors in the program.
Getting Started With C

C is a popular and efficient programming language which is widely used for system and application software. In order to create and run a C program, you need a C-language compiler. There are many free and professional C-language compilers available.

Every C program contains a function called *main( )*. A function is simply a collection of statements that is used to perform some operation. The main function is always called when the program first executes. From main, we can call other functions, whether they are user defined or built-in. To access the standard functions that comes with C compiler, you need to include a header file with the *#include* directive.
2.3.1 Header File

Header files are collection of standard library functions to perform different tasks. There are many header files for different purposes. Each header file contains different types of predefined functions. Many header files can be included in one program. The header file must be included in the program before calling any of its functions in the program.
2.3.1 Header File
The extension of a header file is *.h*. The *#include* preprocessor directive is used to include header files in programs. These files are provided by C compiler system.
2.3.1 Header File
The header files are normally stored in *INCLUDE* subdirectory. The name of header file is written in angle brackets.
2.3.1 Header File

Each header file contains information (or declarations) for a particular group of functions. Like *stdio.h* header file contains declarations of standard input and output functions available in C which is used to get the input and print the output. Similarly, the header file *math.h* contains declarations of mathematical functions available in C.
2.3.2 Reserved words

The words that are used by the language for special purposes are called reserved words or keywords. Each keyword has fixed meaning and that cannot be changed by user. Every Keyword exists in lower case letter like auto, break, case, const, continue, int etc. C Language supports 32 keywords.

3.2.7 Logical Operators
Logical operators are used to evaluate compound conditions. There are three logical operators in C language:
a. AND Operator &&
The symbol used for AND operator is &&. It is used to evaluate two conditions. It produces true result if both conditions are true. It produces false result if any of the conditions is false.
a. AND Operator &&
Condition 1 | Operator | Condition 2 | Result; False | && | False | False; False | && | True | False; True | && | False | False; True | && | True | True
a. AND Operator &&

Example: Suppose we have two variables A =100 and B= 50. The compound condition (A>10) && (B>10) is true, as both the conditions are true. The compound condition (A>50) && (B>50) is false, as the first condition is true but the second is false.
b. OR Operator ||
The symbol used for OR operator is ||. It is used to evaluate two conditions. It produces true result if either of the condition is true. It produces false result if both the conditions are false.
b. OR Operator ||
Condition 1 | Operator | Condition 2 | Result; False | | False | False; False | | True | True

Example: Suppose we have two variables A = 100 and B= 50. The compound condition (A>50) || (B>50) is true, as one condition is true.
c. NOT Operator !

4.1 CONTROL STRUCTURE

Control structures are the basic entities of a structured programming language. Control structures are used to alter the flow of execution of the program. Why do we need to alter the program flow? The reason is "decision making".
4.1 CONTROL STRUCTURE

There come situations in real life when we need to make some decisions and based on these decisions, we decide what we should do next. For example, we may be given different options like doing "Medical" or "Engineering". We do make a decision by analyzing certain conditions (like our personal interest, scope of opportunities etc.) With the decision we make, we alter the flow of our life's direction.
4.1 CONTROL STRUCTURE
Similar situations arise in C programming also where we need to make some decisions and alter the direction of program flow in one or the other path(s) available.
4.1.1 Control Statements

Programs consist of sections or blocks of instructions that sit idle until they are needed. When needed, the program moves to the appropriate section to accomplish a task. While one section of code is busy, the other sections are inactive. Control statements are how programmers indicate which sections of code to use at specific times.
4.1.1 Control Statements

However, depending on the requirements of a problem it might be required to alter the normal sequence of execution in a program. Control statements are elements in the source code that control the flow of program execution. The statements which specify the order of execution of statements are called *Control Statements*. There are two main types of control statements.

5.1 INTRODUCTION

Loops are one of the most powerful concepts of computer programming facilitating the programmers to create such programs that are effective and efficient and to meet the requirement of the business needs. A loop is a sequence of instructions that is continually repeated until a certain condition is reached.
5.1 INTRODUCTION

For example, if a programmer creates a program for payroll processing that needs to compute the salaries and the allowances of 1000 employees in a company. The computer begins to compute the salaries and allowances of all the employees, using a loop, until it accomplishes this task for all the employees.
5.1 INTRODUCTION

Similarly, in order to get print outs of the pay-slips of all the employees in a company requires a loop to be assigned, so that the pay-slips for all the employees can be generated and printed accordingly. If the same activity is done manually, it would take hours and days. Loops, on the other hand, execute the tasks faster saving the time and effort.
5.1 INTRODUCTION
They are also very helpful to accomplish the tasks in an accurate manner. C language offers different types of looping structures.
5.1.1 Loop Structure

In sequential control structure, all statements are executed one after the other. On the other hand, conditional structure may execute or skip a statement on the basis of some given condition. In some situations, it is required to repeat a statement or number of statements for a specified number of times. Looping structures are used for this purpose.

6.1 DATA REPRESENTATION IN A COMPUTER

Data can be defined as a representation of facts, concepts, or instructions in a formalized manner, which should be suitable for communication, interpretation or processing by human or electronic machine. In digital computers, the user input is first converted and transmitted as electrical pulses that can be represented by two unique states ON and OFF. The ON state is represented by "1" and the OFF state by "0".
6.1 DATA REPRESENTATION IN A COMPUTER
The sequence of ON's and OFF's forms the electrical signals that the computer can understand. One digit in binary number system is called a bit and combination of eight bits is called a byte.
6.1 DATA REPRESENTATION IN A COMPUTER

A byte is the basic unit of computer memory that is used to represent data. One byte represents one character of data. It can be an alphabetic character, numeric character or any other special symbol. Data is the combination of characters, numbers and symbols collected for a specific purpose.
6.1 DATA REPRESENTATION IN A COMPUTER

For example, when the letter A is input to the computer it is first converted to its binary code i.e., 01000001. In the same way all other characters in the form of data, are given to the computer for processing.
6.2 LOGIC GATES
Logic gates are the basic building blocks of digital computer. Logic gates are used to carry out logical operations on single or multiple binary inputs 0 and 1 and
6.2 LOGIC GATES

6.2.1 Digital Logic and Logic Gates
Digital logic is used to create digital circuits that consist of large number of logic gates.
6.2.1 Digital Logic and Logic Gates

A Logic Gate is a device that acts as a building block for digital circuits. Logic gates perform basic logical functions that are fundamental to digital circuits. Inside most electronic devices we use today have some form of logic gates. For example, logic gates can be used in technologies such as smartphones, tablets or within memory devices.
6.2.1 Digital Logic and Logic Gates

In a circuit, logic gates make decisions based on a combination of digital signals coming from its inputs. Most logic gates have two inputs and one output. Logic gates are based on Boolean algebra. At any given moment, every terminal is in one of the two binary conditions, false or true. False represents 0, and true represents 1.
6.2.1 Digital Logic and Logic Gates

Depending on the type of logic gate being used and the combination of inputs, the binary output differs. A logic gate can be thought of like a light switch, wherein one position the output is OFF (0), and in another, it is ON (1). Logic gates are commonly used in Integrated Circuits (IC).
6.2.2 Basic Logic Gates

The operation of every single logic gate can be easily understood and is similar to addition and multiplication that we already know in ordinary mathematics. Based on the logical gate, the logical operation differs, and the output varies. Each logic gate follows a truth table that gives the possible combinations of input and the respective obtained output.
6.2.2 Basic Logic Gates

There are several basic logic gates used in performing operations in digital systems. The three basic gates are AND, OR and NOT. These three gates can be used to implement other complex types of gates.

Boolean function simplification

It is the process of reducing the number of terms and/or variables in a Boolean function without affecting the final output. Different methods are used for this purpose. Maurice Karnaugh, a telecommunications engineer, developed the Karnaugh map at Bell Labs in 1953. This is a simple method for simplification of Boolean functions.
Boolean function simplification
When a simplified Boolean function is converted into a logic circuit, it requires less number of gates and hence costs less.
6.3.1 Karnaugh Map (K-Map)

The K-map method of solving the logical expressions is referred to as the graphical technique of simplifying Boolean expressions. K-maps are also referred to as 2D truth tables as each K-map is nothing but a different format of representing the values present in a one-dimensional truth table.
6.3.1 Karnaugh Map (K-Map)

K-maps basically deal with the technique of inserting the values of the output variable in cells within a rectangle or square grid according to a definite pattern. The number of cells in the K-map is determined by the number of input variables and is mathematically expressed as two raised to the power of the number of input variables, i.e., 2ⁿ, where the number of input variables is n.
6.3.1 Karnaugh Map (K-Map)
Thus, to simplify a logical expression with two inputs, we require a K-map with 4 (=2²) cells. A four-input logical expression would lead to a 16 (=2⁴) celled-K-map, and so on.
6.3.1 Karnaugh Map (K-Map)
The diagram below illustrates the correspondence between the Karnaugh map and the truth table for the general case of a two variable problem.
6.3.1 Karnaugh Map (K-Map)

The values inside the squares are copied from the output column of the truth table, therefore, there is one square in the map for every row in the truth table. Around the edge of the Karnaugh map are the values of the two input variables. A is along the top and B is down the left hand side. The diagram below explains this:
6.3.1 Karnaugh Map (K-Map)

As an example, the square on the top right hand corner of the map in the above diagram has A=1 and B=0. This square corresponds to the row in the truth table where A=1, B=0 and F=1. Note that the value in the F column represents a particular function to which the Karnaugh map corresponds.
i. Karnaugh Maps - Rules of Simplification
The Karnaugh map uses the following rules for the simplification of expressions by grouping together adjacent cells containing *ones*.
i. Karnaugh Maps - Rules of Simplification
Groups may not include any cell containing a zero
i. Karnaugh Maps - Rules of Simplification
Groups may be horizontal or vertical, but not diagonal.
i. Karnaugh Maps - Rules of Simplification
Groups must contain 1, 2, 4, 8, or in general 2ⁿ cells.
i. Karnaugh Maps - Rules of Simplification
That is if n = 1, a group will contain two 1's since 2¹ = 2.
i. Karnaugh Maps - Rules of Simplification
If n = 2, a group will contain four 1's since 2² = 4.
i. Karnaugh Maps - Rules of Simplification
Each group should be as large as possible.
i. Karnaugh Maps - Rules of Simplification
Each cell containing a *one* must be in at least one group.
i. Karnaugh Maps - Rules of Simplification
Groups may wrap around the table. The leftmost cell in a row may be grouped with the rightmost cell and the top cell in a column may be grouped with the bottom cell.
i. Karnaugh Maps - Rules of Simplification
There should be as few groups as possible, as long as this does not contradict any of the previous rules.

7.8 CREATING FRAMES

HTML frames are used to divide your browser window into multiple sections where each section can load a separate HTML document. A collection of frames in the browser window is known as a frameset. The window is divided into frames in a similar way the tables are organized: into rows and columns.
7.8.1 Frame

A frame is a small rectangular window or pane within a browser window. Frames allow the user to display more than one HTML document in the same browser window. Each frame is independent of the other. The <frame> tag is used to place an HTML document in a frame.
7.8.2 Frameset

Frameset defines how to divide the browser window into frames. To use frames on a page we use <frameset>. The <frameset> tag defines, how to divide the browser window into vertical frames or horizontal frames.
7.8.3 Creating a Frameset
The <frameset></frameset> and <frame> tags instead of <body> tag are used together to create frames in browser window. The frameset tag is used in the header section and not inside the *body* tag.
7.8.3 Creating a Frameset

The <frameset></frameset> tags define either a series of columns or rows. It has two attributes *cols* and *rows*. The syntax of both attributes is the same. *Cols* defines a series of columns and *rows* defines a series of rows.
7.8.3 Creating a Frameset
<frameset cols=30%, 30%, 40%>
7.8.3 Creating a Frameset
will divide the browser window into three columns. The first two columns will be set to 30% of the width of browser window and the third column to 40%. This will create three vertical frames.

will divide the browser window into two equal-sized rows that is the browser window will be divided into two equal-sized horizontal frames.
7.8.3 Creating a Frameset

Key Points

World Wide Web (www) is an information system on the Internet which allows documents to be connected to other documents by hypertext links, enabling the user to search for information by moving from one document to another. • A web page is a document on the Internet that can be accessed through a web browser. • A website is a collection of related web pages hosted on a web server.
Key Points

• A web browser is software that enables users to retrieve information on the Web. • Web servers are computers that facilitate and deliver web pages from various websites they have. • A URL (Uniform Resource Locator) is the unique address for a file that is accessible on the Internet. • A search engine is a website or software system that allows people to find information on the World Wide Web.
Key Points

• Home page is the main or very first web page of a website. • Web hosting is a service, provided by web hosting companies, to upload websites on web servers. • Web portals are websites that offer different types of services. • News websites provide information about current events and opinions. • Informational websites provide information on any topic in the form of text, graphics, sound and videos.
Key Points

• Educational websites are created for educational purpose. These sites contain animation, slide presentations and tutorials to educate people on various topics. • Personal websites are created and maintained by individuals for personal use. • Business websites provide facilities to maintain business relationships and selling information, services and commodities via Internet.
Key Points
• HTML stands for Hypertext Markup Language. It is used to create web pages. • HTML tag is a command or code that specifies how a web page is formatted.

كَمَا أَخْرَجَكَ رَبُّكَ مِن بَيْتِكَ بِالْحَقِّ وَإِنَّ فَرِيقًا مِّنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ لَكَارِهُونَ ﴿٥﴾ — (ان لوگوں کو اپنے گھروں سے اسی طرح نکلنا چاہیے تھا) جس طرح تمہارے پروردگار نے تم کو تدبیر کے ساتھ اپنے گھر سے نکالا اور (اس وقت) مومنوں کی ایک جماعت ناخوش تھی۔

يُجَادِلُونَكَ فِي الْحَقِّ بَعْدَمَا تَبَيَّنَ كَأَنَّمَا يُسَاقُونَ إِلَى الْمَوْتِ وَهُمْ يَنظُرُونَ ﴿٦﴾ — وہ لوگ حق بات میں اس کے ظاہر ہوئے پیچھے تم سے جھگڑنے لگے گویا موت کی طرف دھکیلے جاتے ہیں اور اسے دیکھ رہے ہیں۔
پہلا سبق (الف) آیات 1 تا 10

وَإِذْ يَعِدُكُمُ اللَّهُ إِحْدَى الطَّائِفَتَيْنِ أَنَّهَا لَكُمْ وَتَوَدُّونَ أَنَّ غَيْرَ ذَاتِ الشَّوْكَةِ تَكُونُ لَكُمْ وَيُرِيدُ اللَّهُ أَن يُحِقَّ الْحَقَّ بِكَلِمَاتِهِ وَيَقْطَعَ دَابِرَ الْكَافِرِينَ ﴿٧﴾ — اور (اس وقت کو یاد کرو) جب اللہ تم سے وعدہ کرتا تھا کہ (ابوسفیان اور ابوجہل کے) دو گروہوں میں سے ایک گروہ تمہارا (مسخر) ہو جائے گا اور تم چاہتے تھے کہ جو قافلہ بے شان و شوکت (یعنی بے ہتھیار) ہے وہ تمہارے ہاتھ آ جائے اور اللہ تو چاہتا تھا کہ اپنے فرمان سے حق کو قائم رکھے اور کافروں کی جڑ کاٹ کر (پھینک) دے۔
پہلا سبق (الف) آیات 1 تا 10
لِيُحِقَّ الْحَقَّ وَيُبْطِلَ الْبَاطِلَ وَلَوْ كَرِهَ الْمُجْرِمُونَ ﴿٨﴾ — تاکہ سچ کو سچ اور جھوٹ کو جھوٹ کر دے، گو مشرک ناخوش ہی ہوں۔
پہلا سبق (الف) آیات 1 تا 10

إِذْ تَسْتَغِيثُونَ رَبَّكُمْ فَاسْتَجَابَ لَكُمْ أَنِّي مُمِدُّكُم بِأَلْفٍ مِّنَ الْمَلَائِكَةِ مُرْدِفِينَ ﴿٩﴾ — جب تم اپنے پروردگار سے فریاد کرتے تھے تو اس نے تمہاری دعا قبول کر لی (اور فرمایا) کہ (تسلی رکھو) ہم ہزار فرشتوں سے جو ایک دوسرے کے پیچھے آتے جائیں گے تمہاری مدد کریں گے۔
پہلا سبق (الف) آیات 1 تا 10

وَمَا جَعَلَهُ اللَّهُ إِلَّا بُشْرَىٰ وَلِتَطْمَئِنَّ بِهِ قُلُوبُكُمْ ۚ وَمَا النَّصْرُ إِلَّا مِنْ عِندِ اللَّهِ ۚ إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَزِيزٌ حَكِيمٌ ﴿١٠﴾ — اور اس مدد کو اللہ نے محض بشارت بنایا تھا کہ تمہارے دل اس سے اطمینان حاصل کریں اور مدد تو اللہ ہی کی طرف سے ہے۔ بے شک خدا غالب حکمت والا ہے۔
اَلْكَلِمَاتُ وَالتَّرَاكِيبُ

اَلْأَنْفَالُ: مالِ غنیمت • أَصْلِحُوا ذَاتَ بَيْنِكُمْ: اپنے آپس کے تعلقات درست رکھو • وَجِلَتْ: ڈر جاتے ہیں، ڈرتے ہیں • كَارِهُونَ: ناگواری محسوس کرنے والے • يُسَاقُونَ: وہ ہانکے جاتے ہیں • إِحْدَى: ایک (مؤنث) • دَابِرَ: جڑ • تَسْتَغِيثُونَ: تم فریاد کرتے ہو • مُرْدِفِينَ: لگاتار آنے والے • غَيْرَ ذَاتِ الشَّوْكَةِ: بغیر کیل کانٹے کے / بغیر اسلحے اور قوت کے
آیات 11 تا 19

إِذْ يُغَشِّيكُمُ النُّعَاسَ أَمَنَةً مِّنْهُ وَيُنَزِّلُ عَلَيْكُم مِّنَ السَّمَاءِ مَاءً لِّيُطَهِّرَكُم بِهِ وَيُذْهِبَ عَنكُمْ رِجْزَ الشَّيْطَانِ وَلِيَرْبِطَ عَلَىٰ قُلُوبِكُمْ وَيُثَبِّتَ بِهِ الْأَقْدَامَ ﴿١١﴾ — جب اس نے تمہاری تسکین کے لیے اپنی طرف سے تمہیں نیند (کی چادر) اڑھا دی اور تم پر آسمان سے پانی برسا دیا کہ تم کو اس سے (نہلا کر) پاک کر دے اور شیطانی نجاست کو تم سے دور کر دے اور اس لیے بھی کہ تمہارے دلوں کو مضبوط کر دے اور اس سے تمہارے پاؤں جمائے رکھے۔
آیات 11 تا 19

إِذْ يُوحِي رَبُّكَ إِلَى الْمَلَائِكَةِ أَنِّي مَعَكُمْ فَثَبِّتُوا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا ۚ سَأُلْقِي فِي قُلُوبِ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا الرُّعْبَ فَاضْرِبُوا فَوْقَ الْأَعْنَاقِ وَاضْرِبُوا مِنْهُمْ كُلَّ بَنَانٍ ﴿١٢﴾ — جب تمہارا پروردگار فرشتوں کو ارشاد فرماتا تھا کہ میں تمہارے ساتھ ہوں تم مومنوں کو تسلی دو کہ ثابت قدم رہیں۔
آیات 11 تا 19
میں ابھی ابھی کافروں کے دلوں میں رعب و ہیبت ڈالے دیتا ہوں تو ان کے سر مار (کر) اڑا دو اور ان کا پور پور مار (کر توڑ) دو۔
آیات 11 تا 19

ذَٰلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمْ شَاقُّوا اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ ۚ وَمَن يُشَاقِقِ اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ شَدِيدُ الْعِقَابِ ﴿١٣﴾ — یہ (سزا) اس لیے دی گئی کہ انھوں نے اللہ اور اس کے رسول ﷺ کی مخالفت کی اور جو شخص اللہ اور اس کے رسول ﷺ کی مخالفت کرتا ہے تو اللہ سخت عذاب دینے والا ہے۔
آیات 11 تا 19
ذَٰلِكُمْ فَذُوقُوهُ وَأَنَّ لِلْكَافِرِينَ عَذَابَ النَّارِ ﴿١٤﴾ — یہ (مزہ تو یہاں) چکھو اور یہ (جانے رہو) کہ کافروں کے لیے (آخرت میں) دوزخ کا عذاب (بھی تیار) ہے۔
آیات 11 تا 19
يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إِذَا لَقِيتُمُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا زَحْفًا فَلَا تُوَلُّوهُمُ الْأَدْبَارَ ﴿١٥﴾ — اے اہلِ ایمان! جب میدانِ جنگ میں کفار سے تمہارا مقابلہ ہو تو ان سے پیٹھ نہ پھیرنا۔
آیات 11 تا 19

وَمَن يُوَلِّهِمْ يَوْمَئِذٍ دُبُرَهُ إِلَّا مُتَحَرِّفًا لِّقِتَالٍ أَوْ مُتَحَيِّزًا إِلَىٰ فِئَةٍ فَقَدْ بَاءَ بِغَضَبٍ مِّنَ اللَّهِ وَمَأْوَاهُ جَهَنَّمُ ۖ وَبِئْسَ الْمَصِيرُ ﴿١٦﴾ — اور جو شخص جنگ کے روز اس صورت کے سوا کہ لڑائی کے لیے کنارے کنارے چلے (یعنی حکمتِ عملی سے دشمن کو مارے) یا اپنی فوج میں جا ملنا چاہے، ان سے پیٹھ پھیرے گا تو (سمجھو کہ) وہ اللہ کے غضب میں گرفتار ہو گیا اور اس کا ٹھکانہ دوزخ ہے اور وہ بہت ہی بری جگہ ہے۔
آیات 11 تا 19

فَلَمْ تَقْتُلُوهُمْ وَلَٰكِنَّ اللَّهَ قَتَلَهُمْ ۚ وَمَا رَمَيْتَ إِذْ رَمَيْتَ وَلَٰكِنَّ اللَّهَ رَمَىٰ ۚ وَلِيُبْلِيَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ مِنْهُ بَلَاءً حَسَنًا ۚ إِنَّ اللَّهَ سَمِيعٌ عَلِيمٌ ﴿١٧﴾ — تم لوگوں نے ان (کفار) کو قتل نہیں کیا بلکہ خدا نے انھیں قتل کیا اور (اے محمد ﷺ) جس وقت تم نے کنکریاں پھینکی تھیں تو وہ تم نے نہیں پھینکی تھیں بلکہ اللہ نے پھینکی تھیں۔
آیات 11 تا 19
اس سے یہ غرض تھی کہ مومنوں کو اپنے (احسانوں) سے اچھی طرح آزما لے۔ بے شک خدا سنتا جانتا ہے۔
آیات 11 تا 19
ذَٰلِكُمْ وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ مُوهِنُ كَيْدِ الْكَافِرِينَ ﴿١٨﴾ — (بات) یہ (ہے) کچھ شک نہیں کہ خدا کافروں کی تدبیر کو کمزور کر دینے والا ہے۔
آیات 11 تا 19

إِن تَسْتَفْتِحُوا فَقَدْ جَاءَكُمُ الْفَتْحُ ۖ وَإِن تَنتَهُوا فَهُوَ خَيْرٌ لَّكُمْ ۖ وَإِن تَعُودُوا نَعُدْ وَلَن تُغْنِيَ عَنكُمْ فِئَتُكُمْ شَيْئًا وَلَوْ كَثُرَتْ وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ مَعَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ ﴿١٩﴾ — (کافرو) اگر تم (محمد رسول اللہ ﷺ پر) فتح چاہتے ہو تو تمہارے پاس فتح آ چکی۔
آیات 11 تا 19

(دیکھو) اگر تم (اپنے افعال سے) باز آ جاؤ تو تمہارے حق میں بہتر ہے اور اگر پھر (نافرمانی) کرو گے تو ہم بھی پھر تمہیں (عذاب) کریں گے اور تمہاری جماعت خواہ کتنی ہی کثیر ہو تمہارے کچھ بھی کام نہ آئے گی اور خدا تو مومنوں کے ساتھ ہے۔
الفاظ و مرکبات کے معانی

يُغَشِّي: وہ ڈھانپ دیتا ہے / طاری کر دیتا ہے • النُّعَاسَ: اونگھ، غنودگی • رِجْزَ الشَّيْطَانِ: شیطان کی نجاست • الْأَعْنَاقِ: گردنیں • بَنَانٍ: پور پور • زَحْفًا: لڑائی کے لیے کنارے کنارے چلے • مُتَحَرِّفًا لِّقِتَالٍ: جنگی چال کے طور پر • مُتَحَيِّزًا إِلَىٰ فِئَةٍ: کسی فوج سے جا ملنے کے لیے • رَمَيْتَ: تو نے پھینکا • لِيُبْلِيَ: تاکہ وہ آزمائے • مُوهِنُ: کمزور کرنے والا
آیات 20 تا 28

يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا أَطِيعُوا اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ وَلَا تَوَلَّوْا عَنْهُ وَأَنتُمْ تَسْمَعُونَ ﴿٢٠﴾ — اے ایمان والو! اللہ اور اس کے رسول ﷺ کے حکم پر چلو اور اس سے روگردانی نہ کرو اور تم سنتے ہو۔
آیات 20 تا 28
وَلَا تَكُونُوا كَالَّذِينَ قَالُوا سَمِعْنَا وَهُمْ لَا يَسْمَعُونَ ﴿٢١﴾ — اور ان لوگوں جیسے نہ ہونا جو کہتے ہیں کہ ہم نے (حکمِ خدا) سن لیا مگر (حقیقت میں) نہیں سنتے۔
آیات 20 تا 28
إِنَّ شَرَّ الدَّوَابِّ عِندَ اللَّهِ الصُّمُّ الْبُكْمُ الَّذِينَ لَا يَعْقِلُونَ ﴿٢٢﴾ — کچھ شک نہیں کہ اللہ کے نزدیک تمام جانداروں سے بدتر بہرے گونگے ہیں جو کچھ نہیں سمجھتے۔
آیات 20 تا 28

وَلَوْ عَلِمَ اللَّهُ فِيهِمْ خَيْرًا لَّأَسْمَعَهُمْ ۖ وَلَوْ أَسْمَعَهُمْ لَتَوَلَّوا وَّهُم مُّعْرِضُونَ ﴿٢٣﴾ — اور اگر اللہ ان میں نیکی (کا مادہ) دیکھتا تو ان کو سننے کی توفیق بخشتا اور اگر بغیر صلاحیتِ ہدایت کے سماعت دیتا تو وہ منہ پھیر کر بھاگ جاتے۔
آیات 20 تا 28

يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اسْتَجِيبُوا لِلَّهِ وَلِلرَّسُولِ إِذَا دَعَاكُمْ لِمَا يُحْيِيكُمْ ۖ وَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّ اللَّهَ يَحُولُ بَيْنَ الْمَرْءِ وَقَلْبِهِ وَأَنَّهُ إِلَيْهِ تُحْشَرُونَ ﴿٢٤﴾ — مومنو!
آیات 20 تا 28

اللہ اور اس کے رسول ﷺ کا حکم قبول کرو جبکہ رسول اللہ ﷺ تمہیں ایسے کام کے لیے بلاتے ہیں جو تم کو زندگی (جاوداں) بخشتا ہے اور جان رکھو کہ اللہ آدمی اور اس کے دل کے درمیان حائل ہو جاتا ہے اور یہ بھی کہ تم سب اس کے روبرو جمع کیے جاؤ گے۔
آیات 20 تا 28

وَاتَّقُوا فِتْنَةً لَّا تُصِيبَنَّ الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا مِنكُمْ خَاصَّةً ۖ وَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّ اللَّهَ شَدِيدُ الْعِقَابِ ﴿٢٥﴾ — اور اس فتنے سے ڈرو جو خصوصیت کے ساتھ ان ہی لوگوں پر واقع نہ ہوگا جو تم میں گناہگار ہیں اور جان رکھو کہ اللہ سخت عذاب دینے والا ہے۔
آیات 20 تا 28

وَاذْكُرُوا إِذْ أَنتُمْ قَلِيلٌ مُّسْتَضْعَفُونَ فِي الْأَرْضِ تَخَافُونَ أَن يَتَخَطَّفَكُمُ النَّاسُ فَآوَاكُمْ وَأَيَّدَكُم بِنَصْرِهِ وَرَزَقَكُم مِّنَ الطَّيِّبَاتِ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَشْكُرُونَ ﴿٢٦﴾ — اور (اس وقت کو) یاد کرو جب تم زمین (مکہ) میں قلیل اور ضعیف سمجھے جاتے تھے اور ڈرتے رہتے تھے کہ لوگ تمہیں اُڑا (نہ) لے جائیں (یعنی بے خانماں نہ کر دیں) اور اس نے تم کو جگہ دی اور اپنی مدد سے تم کو تقویت بخشی اور پاکیزہ چیزیں کھانے کو دیں تاکہ (اس کا) شکر کرو۔
آیات 20 تا 28

يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لَا تَخُونُوا اللَّهَ وَالرَّسُولَ وَتَخُونُوا أَمَانَاتِكُمْ وَأَنتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ ﴿٢٧﴾ — ایمان والو! نہ تو اللہ اور رسول ﷺ کی امانت میں خیانت کرو اور نہ اپنی امانتوں میں خیانت کرو اور تم (ان باتوں کو) جانتے ہو۔
آیات 20 تا 28

وَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّمَا أَمْوَالُكُمْ وَأَوْلَادُكُمْ فِتْنَةٌ وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ عِندَهُ أَجْرٌ عَظِيمٌ ﴿٢٨﴾ — اور جان رکھو کہ تمہارا مال اور اولاد بڑی آزمائش ہے اور یہ کہ اللہ کے پاس (نیکیوں کا) بڑا ثواب ہے۔
الفاظ و مرکبات کے معانی

شَرَّ الدَّوَابِّ: جانوروں میں سب سے بدترین • اسْتَجِيبُوا: حکم مانو، پکار کا جواب دو • يَحُولُ: حائل ہوتا ہے • مُّسْتَضْعَفُونَ: مغلوب، کمزور • يَتَخَطَّفَ: وہ اچک لے اڑائے • لَا تَخُونُوا: تم خیانت نہ کرو
آیات 29 تا 37

يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إِن تَتَّقُوا اللَّهَ يَجْعَل لَّكُمْ فُرْقَانًا وَيُكَفِّرْ عَنكُمْ سَيِّئَاتِكُمْ وَيَغْفِرْ لَكُمْ ۗ وَاللَّهُ ذُو الْفَضْلِ الْعَظِيمِ ﴿٢٩﴾ — مومنو! اگر تم اللہ سے ڈرو گے تو وہ تمہارے لیے امرِ فارق پیدا کر دے گا (یعنی تم کو ممتاز کر دے گا) اور تمہارے گناہ مٹا دے گا اور تمہیں بخش دے گا اور اللہ بڑے فضل والا ہے۔
آیات 29 تا 37

وَإِذْ يَمْكُرُ بِكَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لِيُثْبِتُوكَ أَوْ يَقْتُلُوكَ أَوْ يُخْرِجُوكَ ۚ وَيَمْكُرُونَ وَيَمْكُرُ اللَّهُ ۖ وَاللَّهُ خَيْرُ الْمَاكِرِينَ ﴿٣٠﴾ — اور (اے محمد ﷺ اس وقت کو یاد کرو) جب کافر لوگ تمہارے بارے میں چال چل رہے تھے کہ تم کو قید کر دیں یا جان سے مار ڈالیں یا (وطن سے) نکال دیں تو (ادھر تو) وہ چال چل رہے تھے اور (ادھر) اللہ چال چل رہا تھا اور خدا سب سے بہتر چال چلنے والا ہے۔
آیات 29 تا 37

وَإِذَا تُتْلَىٰ عَلَيْهِمْ آيَاتُنَا قَالُوا قَدْ سَمِعْنَا لَوْ نَشَاءُ لَقُلْنَا مِثْلَ هَٰذَا ۙ إِنْ هَٰذَا إِلَّا أَسَاطِيرُ الْأَوَّلِينَ ﴿٣١﴾ — اور جب ان کو ہماری آیتیں پڑھ کر سنائی جاتی ہیں تو کہتے ہیں (یہ کلام) ہم نے سن لیا ہے اگر ہم چاہتے تو اسی طرح کا (کلام) ہم بھی کہہ دیتے اور یہ ہے ہی کیا صرف اگلے لوگوں کی حکایتیں ہیں۔
آیات 29 تا 37

وَإِذْ قَالُوا اللَّهُمَّ إِن كَانَ هَٰذَا هُوَ الْحَقَّ مِنْ عِندِكَ فَأَمْطِرْ عَلَيْنَا حِجَارَةً مِّنَ السَّمَاءِ أَوِ ائْتِنَا بِعَذَابٍ أَلِيمٍ ﴿٣٢﴾ — اور جب انھوں نے کہا کہ اے اللہ اگر یہ (قرآن) تیری طرف سے برحق ہے تو ہم پر آسمان سے پتھر برسا یا کوئی اور تکلیف دینے والا عذاب بھیج۔
آیات 29 تا 37

وَمَا كَانَ اللَّهُ لِيُعَذِّبَهُمْ وَأَنتَ فِيهِمْ ۚ وَمَا كَانَ اللَّهُ مُعَذِّبَهُمْ وَهُمْ يَسْتَغْفِرُونَ ﴿٣٣﴾ — اور اللہ ایسا نہ تھا کہ جب تک تم ان میں تھے انھیں عذاب دیتا اور نہ ایسا تھا کہ وہ بخشش مانگیں اور انھیں عذاب دے۔
آیات 29 تا 37
وَمَا لَهُمْ أَلَّا يُعَذِّبَهُمُ اللَّهُ — اور (اب) ان کے لیے کون سی وجہ ہے کہ وہ انھیں عذاب نہ دے۔ (آیت اگلے صفحے پر جاری ہے)
آیات 29 تا 37

وَهُمْ يَصُدُّونَ عَنِ الْمَسْجِدِ الْحَرَامِ وَمَا كَانُوا أَوْلِيَاءَهُ ۚ إِنْ أَوْلِيَاؤُهُ إِلَّا الْمُتَّقُونَ وَلَٰكِنَّ أَكْثَرَهُمْ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ ﴿٣٤﴾ — جب کہ وہ مسجدِ محترم میں (نماز پڑھنے) سے روکتے ہیں اور وہ اس مسجد کے متولی بھی نہیں اور اس کے متولی تو صرف پرہیزگار ہیں لیکن ان میں سے اکثر نہیں جانتے۔
آیات 29 تا 37

وَمَا كَانَ صَلَاتُهُمْ عِندَ الْبَيْتِ إِلَّا مُكَاءً وَتَصْدِيَةً ۚ فَذُوقُوا الْعَذَابَ بِمَا كُنتُمْ تَكْفُرُونَ ﴿٣٥﴾ — اور ان لوگوں کی نماز خانہ کعبہ کے پاس سیٹیاں اور تالیاں بجانے کے سوا کچھ نہ تھی تو تم جو کفر کرتے تھے اب اس کے بدلے عذاب کا مزہ چکھو۔
آیات 29 تا 37

إِنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا يُنفِقُونَ أَمْوَالَهُمْ لِيَصُدُّوا عَن سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ ۚ فَسَيُنفِقُونَهَا ثُمَّ تَكُونُ عَلَيْهِمْ حَسْرَةً ثُمَّ يُغْلَبُونَ ۗ — جو لوگ کافر ہیں اپنا مال خرچ کرتے ہیں کہ (لوگوں کو) اللہ کے راستے سے روکیں سو ابھی اور خرچ کریں گے مگر آخر وہ (خرچ کرنا) ان کے لیے (موجبِ) افسوس ہوگا اور وہ مغلوب ہو جائیں گے۔
آیات 29 تا 37

وَالَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا إِلَىٰ جَهَنَّمَ يُحْشَرُونَ ﴿٣٦﴾ لِيَمِيزَ اللَّهُ الْخَبِيثَ مِنَ الطَّيِّبِ وَيَجْعَلَ الْخَبِيثَ بَعْضَهُ عَلَىٰ بَعْضٍ فَيَرْكُمَهُ جَمِيعًا فَيَجْعَلَهُ فِي جَهَنَّمَ ۚ أُولَٰئِكَ هُمُ الْخَاسِرُونَ ﴿٣٧﴾ — اور کافر لوگ دوزخ کی طرف ہانکے جائیں گے تاکہ اللہ ناپاک کو پاک سے الگ کر دے اور ناپاک کو ایک دوسرے پر رکھ کر ایک ڈھیر بنا دے، پھر اس کو دوزخ میں ڈال دے۔ یہی لوگ خسارہ پانے والے ہیں۔
الفاظ و مرکبات کے معانی
لِيُثْبِتُوكَ: وہ قید کر دیں • أَسَاطِيرُ الْأَوَّلِينَ: پہلوں کی کہانیاں • مُكَاءً: سیٹیاں • تَصْدِيَةً: تالیاں • فَيَرْكُمَهُ: وہ جمع کرے اسے
آیات 38 تا 44

قُل لِّلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا إِن يَنتَهُوا يُغْفَرْ لَهُم مَّا قَدْ سَلَفَ وَإِن يَعُودُوا فَقَدْ مَضَتْ سُنَّتُ الْأَوَّلِينَ ﴿٣٨﴾ — (اے پیغمبر ﷺ) کفار سے کہہ دو کہ اگر وہ اپنے افعال سے باز آ جائیں تو جو ہو چکا وہ انھیں معاف کر دیا جائے گا اور اگر پھر (وہی حرکات) کرنے لگیں گے تو اگلے لوگوں کا (جو) طریق جاری ہو چکا ہے (وہی ان کے حق میں برتا جائے گا)۔
آیات 38 تا 44

وَقَاتِلُوهُمْ حَتَّىٰ لَا تَكُونَ فِتْنَةٌ وَيَكُونَ الدِّينُ كُلُّهُ لِلَّهِ ۚ فَإِنِ انتَهَوْا فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ بِمَا يَعْمَلُونَ بَصِيرٌ ﴿٣٩﴾ — اور ان لوگوں سے لڑتے رہو یہاں تک کہ فتنہ (کفر کا فساد) باقی نہ رہے اور دین سب اللہ ہی کا ہو جائے اور اگر باز آ جائیں تو اللہ ان کے کاموں کو دیکھ رہا ہے۔
آیات 38 تا 44
وَإِن تَوَلَّوْا فَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّ اللَّهَ مَوْلَاكُمْ ۚ نِعْمَ الْمَوْلَىٰ وَنِعْمَ النَّصِيرُ ﴿٤٠﴾ — اور اگر روگردانی کریں تو جان رکھو کہ اللہ تمہارا حمایتی ہے اور وہ خوب حمایتی اور خوب مددگار ہے۔
آیات 38 تا 44

وَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّمَا غَنِمْتُم مِّن شَيْءٍ فَأَنَّ لِلَّهِ خُمُسَهُ وَلِلرَّسُولِ وَلِذِي الْقُرْبَىٰ وَالْيَتَامَىٰ وَالْمَسَاكِينِ وَابْنِ السَّبِيلِ إِن كُنتُمْ آمَنتُم بِاللَّهِ وَمَا أَنزَلْنَا عَلَىٰ عَبْدِنَا يَوْمَ الْفُرْقَانِ يَوْمَ الْتَقَى الْجَمْعَانِ ۗ وَاللَّهُ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ ﴿٤١﴾ — اور جان رکھو کہ جو چیز تم کو (کفار سے) غنیمت ملے اس میں سے پانچواں حصہ اللہ کا اور اس کے رسول ﷺ کا اور اہلِ قرابت کا اور یتیموں کا اور محتاجوں کا اور مسافروں کا ہے۔
آیات 38 تا 44

اگر تم اللہ پر اور اس (نصرت) پر ایمان رکھتے ہو جو (حق و باطل میں) فرق کرنے کے دن (یعنی جنگِ بدر میں) جس دن دونوں فوجوں میں مڈھ بھیڑ ہو گئی اپنے بندے (محمد ﷺ) پر نازل فرمائی اور اللہ ہر چیز پر قادر ہے۔
آیات 38 تا 44

إِذْ أَنتُم بِالْعُدْوَةِ الدُّنْيَا وَهُم بِالْعُدْوَةِ الْقُصْوَىٰ وَالرَّكْبُ أَسْفَلَ مِنكُمْ ۚ وَلَوْ تَوَاعَدتُّمْ لَاخْتَلَفْتُمْ فِي الْمِيعَادِ ۙ وَلَٰكِن لِّيَقْضِيَ اللَّهُ أَمْرًا كَانَ مَفْعُولًا لِّيَهْلِكَ مَنْ هَلَكَ عَن بَيِّنَةٍ وَيَحْيَىٰ مَنْ حَيَّ عَن بَيِّنَةٍ ۗ وَإِنَّ اللَّهَ لَسَمِيعٌ عَلِيمٌ ﴿٤٢﴾ — جس وقت تم (مدینے سے) قریب کے ناکے پر تھے اور کافر بعید کے ناکے پر اور قافلہ تم سے نیچے اتر گیا
آیات 38 تا 44

تھا اور اگر تم (جنگ کے لیے) آپس میں قرارداد کر لیتے تو وقتِ معین (پر جمع ہونے) میں تقدیم و تاخیر ہو جاتی لیکن اللہ کو منظور تھا کہ جو کام ہو کر رہنے والا تھا اسے کر ہی ڈالے تاکہ جو مرے بصیرت پر (یعنی یقین جان کر) مرے اور جو جیتا رہے وہ بھی بصیرت پر (حق پہچان کر) جیتا رہے اور کچھ شک نہیں کہ اللہ سنتا اور جانتا ہے۔
آیات 38 تا 44

إِذْ يُرِيكَهُمُ اللَّهُ فِي مَنَامِكَ قَلِيلًا ۖ وَلَوْ أَرَاكَهُمْ كَثِيرًا لَّفَشِلْتُمْ وَلَتَنَازَعْتُمْ فِي الْأَمْرِ وَلَٰكِنَّ اللَّهَ سَلَّمَ ۗ إِنَّهُ عَلِيمٌ بِذَاتِ الصُّدُورِ ﴿٤٣﴾ — اس وقت اللہ نے تمہیں خواب میں کافروں کو تھوڑی تعداد میں دکھایا اور اگر بہت کر کے دکھاتا تو تم لوگ جی چھوڑ دیتے اور جو کام درپیش تھا اس میں جھگڑنے لگتے لیکن اللہ نے (تمھیں اس سے) بچا لیا۔ بے شک وہ سینوں کی باتوں تک سے واقف ہے۔
آیات 38 تا 44

وَإِذْ يُرِيكُمُوهُمْ إِذِ الْتَقَيْتُمْ فِي أَعْيُنِكُمْ قَلِيلًا وَيُقَلِّلُكُمْ فِي أَعْيُنِهِمْ لِيَقْضِيَ اللَّهُ أَمْرًا كَانَ مَفْعُولًا ۗ وَإِلَى اللَّهِ تُرْجَعُ الْأُمُورُ ﴿٤٤﴾ — اور اس وقت جب تم ایک دوسرے کے مقابل ہوئے تو کافروں کو تمہاری نظر میں تھوڑا کر کے دکھاتا تھا اور تم کو ان کی نگاہوں میں تھوڑا کر کے دکھاتا تھا تاکہ اللہ کو جو کام کرنا منظور تھا اسے کر ڈالے اور سب کاموں کا رجوع اللہ ہی کی طرف ہے۔
الفاظ و مرکبات کے معانی

مَضَتْ: گزر چکی • يَوْمَ الْفُرْقَانِ: فیصلے کا دن • بِالْعُدْوَةِ الدُّنْيَا: وادی کے اس جانب و کنارے • بِالْعُدْوَةِ الْقُصْوَىٰ: اُس جانب، اُس کنارے • الرَّكْبُ: قافلہ • لَفَشِلْتُمْ: تم ضرور ہمت ہار جاتے • يُقَلِّلُ: تھوڑا کر کے دکھاتا ہے
آیات 45 تا 48

يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إِذَا لَقِيتُمْ فِئَةً فَاثْبُتُوا وَاذْكُرُوا اللَّهَ كَثِيرًا لَّعَلَّكُمْ تُفْلِحُونَ ﴿٤٥﴾ — مومنو! جب (کفار کی) کسی جماعت سے تمہارا مقابلہ ہو تو ثابت قدم رہو اور اللہ کو بہت یاد کرو تاکہ مراد حاصل کرو۔
آیات 45 تا 48

وَأَطِيعُوا اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ وَلَا تَنَازَعُوا فَتَفْشَلُوا وَتَذْهَبَ رِيحُكُمْ ۖ وَاصْبِرُوا ۚ إِنَّ اللَّهَ مَعَ الصَّابِرِينَ ﴿٤٦﴾ — اور اللہ اور اس کے رسول ﷺ کے حکم پر چلو اور آپس میں جھگڑا نہ کرنا کہ (ایسا کرو گے) تو تم بزدل ہو جاؤ گے اور تمہارا اقبال جاتا رہے گا اور صبر سے کام لو کہ اللہ صبر کرنے والوں کا مددگار ہے۔
آیات 45 تا 48

وَلَا تَكُونُوا كَالَّذِينَ خَرَجُوا مِن دِيَارِهِم بَطَرًا وَرِئَاءَ النَّاسِ وَيَصُدُّونَ عَن سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ ۚ وَاللَّهُ بِمَا يَعْمَلُونَ مُحِيطٌ ﴿٤٧﴾ — اور ان لوگوں جیسے نہ ہونا جو اتراتے ہوئے (یعنی حق کا مقابلہ کرنے کے لیے) اور لوگوں کو دکھانے کے لیے گھروں سے نکل آئے اور لوگوں کو اللہ کی راہ سے روکتے ہیں اور جو اعمال یہ کرتے ہیں اللہ ان پر احاطہ کیے ہوئے ہے۔
آیات 45 تا 48

وَإِذْ زَيَّنَ لَهُمُ الشَّيْطَانُ أَعْمَالَهُمْ وَقَالَ لَا غَالِبَ لَكُمُ الْيَوْمَ مِنَ النَّاسِ وَإِنِّي جَارٌ لَّكُمْ ۖ فَلَمَّا تَرَاءَتِ الْفِئَتَانِ نَكَصَ عَلَىٰ عَقِبَيْهِ وَقَالَ إِنِّي بَرِيءٌ مِّنكُمْ إِنِّي أَرَىٰ مَا لَا تَرَوْنَ إِنِّي أَخَافُ اللَّهَ ۚ وَاللَّهُ شَدِيدُ الْعِقَابِ ﴿٤٨﴾ — اور جب شیطانوں نے ان کے اعمال ان کو آراستہ کر کے دکھائے اور کہا کہ آج کے دن لوگوں میں سے کوئی تم پر غالب نہ ہوگا اور میں تمہارا رفیق ہوں لیکن جب دونوں فوجیں ایک دوسرے کے مقابل (صف آرا) ہوئیں تو پسپا ہو کر چل دیا اور کہنے لگا کہ مجھے تم سے کوئی واسطہ نہیں۔
آیات 45 تا 48
میں تو ایسی چیزیں دیکھ رہا ہوں جو تم نہیں دیکھ سکتے۔ مجھے تو اللہ سے ڈر لگتا ہے اور اللہ سخت عذاب کرنے والا ہے۔
الفاظ و مرکبات کے معانی
فَاثْبُتُوا: تم ثابت قدم رہو • فَتَفْشَلُوا: تم بزدل ہو جاؤ گے • بَطَرًا: اتراتے ہوئے • جَارٌ: رفیق / ہمسایہ • تَرَاءَتْ: آمنے سامنے ہوئے • نَكَصَ عَلَىٰ عَقِبَيْهِ: وہ الٹے پاؤں پھر گیا
آیات 49 تا 58

إِذْ يَقُولُ الْمُنَافِقُونَ وَالَّذِينَ فِي قُلُوبِهِم مَّرَضٌ غَرَّ هَٰؤُلَاءِ دِينُهُمْ ۗ وَمَن يَتَوَكَّلْ عَلَى اللَّهِ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ عَزِيزٌ حَكِيمٌ ﴿٤٩﴾ — اس وقت منافق اور (کافر) جن کے دلوں میں مرض تھا کہتے تھے کہ ان لوگوں کو ان کے دین نے مغرور کر رکھا ہے اور جو شخص اللہ پر بھروسا رکھتا ہے تو اللہ غالب حکمت والا ہے۔
آیات 49 تا 58

وَلَوْ تَرَىٰ إِذْ يَتَوَفَّى الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا ۙ الْمَلَائِكَةُ يَضْرِبُونَ وُجُوهَهُمْ وَأَدْبَارَهُمْ وَذُوقُوا عَذَابَ الْحَرِيقِ ﴿٥٠﴾ — اور کاش تم اس وقت (کی کیفیت) دیکھو جب فرشتے کافروں کی جانیں نکالتے ہیں ان کے مونہوں اور پیٹھوں پر (کوڑے اور ہتھوڑے وغیرہ) مارتے (ہیں اور کہتے ہیں) کہ (اب) عذابِ آتش (کا مزہ) چکھو۔
آیات 49 تا 58
ذَٰلِكَ بِمَا قَدَّمَتْ أَيْدِيكُمْ وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ لَيْسَ بِظَلَّامٍ لِّلْعَبِيدِ ﴿٥١﴾ — یہ ان (اعمال) کی سزا ہے جو تمہارے ہاتھوں نے آگے بھیجے ہیں اور یہ (جان رکھو) کہ اللہ بندوں پر ظلم نہیں کرتا۔
آیات 49 تا 58

كَدَأْبِ آلِ فِرْعَوْنَ ۙ وَالَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِهِمْ ۚ كَفَرُوا بِآيَاتِ اللَّهِ فَأَخَذَهُمُ اللَّهُ بِذُنُوبِهِمْ ۗ إِنَّ اللَّهَ قَوِيٌّ شَدِيدُ الْعِقَابِ ﴿٥٢﴾ — جیسا حال فرعونیوں کا اور ان سے پہلے لوگوں کا (ہوا تھا ویسا ہی ان کا ہوا کہ) انھوں نے اللہ کی آیتوں سے کفر کیا تو اللہ نے ان کے گناہوں کی سزا میں ان کو پکڑ لیا۔ بے شک اللہ زبردست اور سخت عذاب دینے والا ہے۔
آیات 49 تا 58
